newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian, Chechen officials hold talks.
newsitem.headline: Russian, Chechen officials hold talks.

text.p: The secretary of Russia's Security Council visited the breakaway region of Chechnya on Wednesday for talks with local leaders.
Ivan Rybkin and his deputy, Boris Berezovsky, travelled to the Chechen capital, Grozny, which has declared itself independent from Moscow and elected a president in January.
Reporters saw Chechnya's First Deputy Prime Minister Movladi Udugov greet the two Russians at the airport. They did not answer questions about their talks.
Russian media reports that Rybkin met Chechen President Aslan Maskhadov could not be confirmed.

Russian news agencies said Udugov returned with Rybkin and Berezovsky to Moscow to continue negotiations on a lasting peace deal in the region. A Security Council official said he could not confirm the reports.

The talks follow Maskhadov's accusations last week that Moscow was continuing a "war" against the region with an economic blockade. He also said Chechnya would not demobilise its guerrilla army until Moscow signed a lasting peace treaty.
The last of Russia's troops left Chechnya early this year after fighting a brutal 20-month war against Chechen separatists that left tens of thousands dead.

In a sign that Moscow wanted to appear to maintain ties with the region, the Russian Finance Ministry, acting on orders from Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, sent five billion roubles ($870,000) to Chechnya for children's welfare, Interfax news agency reported.

Also on Wednesday, however, Ekho Moskvy radio station said Maskhadov's vice-president had ordered fighters into the neighbouring Dagestan region of Russia in support of local ethnic Chechens in a dispute with regional officials.
The report could not be independently confirmed in Chechnya. Officials in Dagestan could not be reached for comment.
